children: Kavaljer Quality Focus gained 2.7% in August, compared with 1.9% for the Stockholm Stock Exchange and 2.6% for the small-cap index. The largest positive contributors during the month were Vitec, Brdr. A&O Johansen and Valmet, while RevolutionRace, New Wave and Catella detracted the most from performance.
Improving sentiment towards high-quality small-cap companies

August was a strong month for equity markets, and we are now seeing early signs of sentiment shifting in favour of high-quality small-cap stocks, which have long been overlooked in favour of large-cap companies. Among other things, brokers who previously contacted us primarily with selling interest are now approaching us with buying interest, suggesting that institutional capital is beginning to return to the segment. We are also seeing early signs of an improving economic environment, which we believe could generate long-awaited revenue growth and stronger profitability going forward.

The fund acted in line with this view during the month. The entire holding in Protector Forsikring was divested and the position in Storytel was reduced, while the fund increased its holdings in RevolutionRace, Proact, ITAB, Securitas, New Wave, Firefly and ChemoMetec. At the end of the month, the equity exposure amounted to 99%.
In-depth review of the fund’s holdings

This month’s in-depth review covers, among other topics, the end of the selling pressure in ITAB from John Fredriksen’s company WQZ, Xvivo’s CE marking for its XHAT heart transplantation solution, AOJ’s acquisition of Elektroimportøren and the recovery in Nederman’s order intake. We also examine Catella’s cost savings and expected acquisitions, Carasent’s strong growth in recurring revenue, and the reasons behind our decision to exit Protector Forsikring following substantial insider selling and signs of a softening market.
Read the full monthly report in the attached file.
